title: What Though No Flowers the Fig-tree Clothe
description: What Though No Flowers the Fig-tree Clothe in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 629 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Rejoicing in Adversity”, where the book credits them to Burder's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: What though no flowers the fig tree clothe Though vines their fruit de-ny, The la-bor of the o-live fail, And fields no meat sup-ply;

lines: What though no flowers the fig-tree clothe
The labor of the olive fail,
Though from the fold, with sad surprise,
My flock cut off I see;
Though famine reign in empty stalls,
Where herds were wont to be; —
Yet in the Lord will I be glad,
In him I'll joy, who will the God
God is the treasure of my soul,
A joy which want shall not impair,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
